Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

upper adjective

also higher (of two), the upper part, upper lip, upstream

classical

Cic. Att. 12.10: tōta domus superior vacat (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 7.46: superiōrem partem collis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 58: upper lip, labrum superius

superior, superius

adjective, comparative of superus; genitive superiōris · Declension on Wiktionary

upper, higher

The upper of two, or the higher part of a thing: labrum superius, the upper lip; in superiōre parte, upstream (Plin. Ep. 8.8.6). Also earlier, former (superiōre annō), and stronger, victorious (Lewis & Short). The i is a vowel.

Other words

  • superus, supera, superum — that is above, upper

    also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 5.1.1: līmen superum inferumque (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The positive, rarer in this plain sense: līmen superum, the lintel; superī, the gods above, and the living. The superlative summus is the top of a thing (see surface).

Examples

  • ad rīvum eundem lupus et agnus vēnerant sitī compulsī; superior stābat lupus longēque īnferior agnus

    a wolf and a lamb had come to the same stream, driven by thirst; the wolf stood higher up, and the lamb far belowPhaedr. 1.1.1–3

  • in superiōre parte nāvigāre tantum, īnfrā etiam natāre concessum

    in the upper part only boating is allowed; lower down you may swim as wellPlin. Ep. 8.8.6

  • tōta domus superior vacat

    the whole upper part of the house is emptyCic. Att. 12.10 (Lewis & Short)

See also upper floor, upper arm, top, above, surface.
